prompt: What is the name of the in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n)?
answer:
The algorithm is **block sort**, commonly represented by the **WikiSort** implementation. It is a stable, in-place comparison sort with:

- **Best case:** \(O(n)\)
- **Worst case:** \(O(n\log n)\)
- **Extra space:** \(O(1)\) (or \(O(\log n)\), depending on implementation details)

Timsort also has \(O(n)\) best-case and \(O(n\log n)\) worst-case time, but it generally requires \(O(n)\) auxiliary memory and is therefore not strictly in-place.
